# Real-time lunar frame / Earth-orientation (EOP) prediction budget.
#
# A lunar navigation frame realised from an Earth-based UT1/polar-motion product is only as good
# as the PREDICTED Earth orientation available in real time: the final IERS values for a given day
# are published weeks later, so an operational service runs on the Bulletin A prediction. This
# scenario emits the two P4 tables (src/frame_eop.rs):
#
#   Table 1 (frame-error consistency): the post-processed (definitive, zero-latency) ~0.27 m frame
#     position and the real-time (predicted, one-hour latency) ~14.4 m frame position, each
#     expressed as its equivalent UT1 error via the L19 lever arm Dr = D_EM * omega_earth * dUT1 —
#     0.27 m <-> ~0.010 ms and 14.4 m <-> ~0.51 ms. The ~14.4 m is the GENUINE propagation of a
#     round representative OD covariance (0.27 m / 4 mm/s) through the one-hour latency — NOT
#     back-solved to hit 15 m; the order-15-m scale is independently bracketed by the real EOP-
#     prediction curve (Table 2: ~9.9 m at 1 day, ~18.8 m at 2 days).
#   Table 2 (UT1 prediction error vs horizon): the L18 curve read directly off the real IERS
#     finals2000A series — the Bulletin A minus Bulletin B final floor and the multi-day
#     persistence-predictor error — each mapped to a Moon-frame position by L19.
#
# It also reports the L21 root-sum-square real-time frame-error budget (EOP + ephemeris + frame-
# realisation floor). The frame-realisation floor is DERIVED from an actual 7-parameter Helmert
# datum realisation (its post-fit RMS residual), and the polar-motion term is sourced from the
# measured Bulletin-A-minus-Bulletin-B pole residual when a real EOP series is supplied.
#
# A plain run emits <scenario>.table.csv — the P4 Table 1 + Table 2 reproducibility artifact
# (byte-stable, golden-pinned in tests/golden/realtime-frame-eop.csv).
#
# Honesty: VALIDATED closed form (the L19 lever arm, omega_earth cross-checked against the CIO
# Earth-rotation angle) and VALIDATED real data (the L18 UT1 and polar-motion curves off the real
# finals2000A rows). DERIVED frame-realisation floor (the Helmert post-fit residual). MODELLED are
# the lunar-relay OD covariance magnitudes (0.27 m post-processed, ~14.4 m real-time at one-hour
# latency — a round, not back-solved, allocation), and the multi-day predictor is persistence, not
# IERS's operational Bulletin A algorithm. Not a certified real-time frame product.
kind = "realtime-frame-eop"

# THE EOP INPUT. Always a REAL IERS finals2000A product, used verbatim. With no path the
# library's own embedded copy of the 2026 extract (tools/finals2000A_2026.txt, MJD 61173-61204)
# is in force: 20 rows carry a Bulletin B final block and 12 are Bulletin A PREDICTION-ONLY rows
# (MJD 61193-61204), so a bare run reports `predicted_rows.n` = 12 and a populated
# `table2_error_vs_horizon` with no file argument and no network (G12).
#
# Other verbatim extracts committed with the repository, for `eop_finals2000a`:
#
#   eop_finals2000a = "tests/fixtures/agency/eop/finals2000A_2022001_longspan.txt"   # 45 final rows
#   eop_finals2000a = "tests/fixtures/agency/eop/finals2000A_2022001.txt"            # 5 final rows
#                                                                                    # (the pre-G12 default)
#
# Both of those are FINAL-ONLY: every row carries a Bulletin B block, so they publish no Bulletin A
# prediction row and `predicted_rows.n` is 0 on them. That zero is the FILE's property, not a
# parser failure, and it stays exercised by test. Moving the default onto the 2026 extract moved
# ten cells of the released p4_frame_eop.csv; they are enumerated old-to-new in
# docs/revisions/G12-default-eop-cell-changes.md under programme rule R4. The emitted `eop_input`
# block names whichever input is actually in force and carries its row census.
#
# `eop_finals2000a_later` takes an ARCHIVED LATER VINTAGE of the same product — the file as it
# stood once the dates the first file predicts had become Bulletin B final. Supplying it turns on
# the true predicted-vs-final vintage differencing. Without it, `table4_predicted_vs_final_horizon`
# is emitted with no rows and says so explicitly: a single instantaneous fetch predicts only dates
# that have no final yet, so the residual does not exist and none is synthesised.
#
# The defaults below reproduce the representative lunar-relay OD covariance (0.27 m / ~14.4 m) and
# the P4 markers; uncomment to override.
epoch = "2022-01-01"
horizons_days = [1, 2, 3]

# latency_s = 3600.0
# frame_realization_floor_m = 0.2  # explicit override; default is DERIVED from the Helmert residual
# frame_realization_tie_noise_m = 0.2
# delta_ut1_ms = 0.5
# delta_xp_mas = 0.0
# delta_yp_mas = 0.0
# eop_finals2000a = "tests/fixtures/agency/eop/finals2000A_2022001_longspan.txt"
# eop_finals2000a_later = "<archived later vintage of the SAME product>"

# THE OPERATIONAL-STYLE PREDICTOR (Table 5 + Table 6).
#
# Table 2's multi-day curve is PERSISTENCE ("tomorrow's UT1 is today's"), which is not what an
# operational user runs on: they consume the IERS Bulletin A prediction. Table 5 adds the class of
# model Bulletin A uses — a least-squares bias + rate fit over a trailing window plus the principal
# periodic terms (annual, semi-annual and the two principal zonal tides for UT1; the Chandler
# wobble, annual and semi-annual for the pole), extrapolated, with the last in-window residual
# carried forward — and scores it PREDICTED-VERSUS-FINAL: a forecast for T+h built only from rapid
# Bulletin A rows at or before T, measured against the LATER-PUBLISHED Bulletin B final at T+h.
# Persistence is scored over the identical epochs against the identical finals beside it, so the
# two columns differ in the predictor and in nothing else. Both are reported; neither replaces the
# other, and Table 2 is unchanged.
#
# IERS fits 365 days. No series committed with this repository is close to that, so the default
# window is 15 days: at most 19 so BOTH committed real extracts can populate it (the 2026 extract
# spans 19 days of finals), and at least ~13.8 so the monthly zonal tide clears the half-cycle
# admission threshold. A term the window cannot constrain is REPORTED as rejected, with the cycles
# the window spans, rather than silently dropped. The bundled 2026 default spans 19 days of
# finals, so a bare run populates Table 5. The 5-row finals2000A_2022001 excerpt supports no
# complete window at all, and on that input Table 5 reports `insufficient-data` and says why.
#
# operational_window_days = 15.0          # 365.0 against a real year-long product
# operational_min_cycle_fraction = 0.5    # cycles of a period the window must span to admit it
# operational_anchor_residual = true      # false gives the bare least-squares extrapolation
